text.p: Italian debt markets failed to haul themselves out of a Monday morning depression in late business after speculation of a possible delay in EMU.

"This EMU delay talk is depressing the market and the lira," one broker in London. Others said some edginess was also apparent due to comments over the weekend from hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti.

The lira floundered most of the day around the 994 per mark area while the June Btp future on LIFFE was 35 basis points down at 127.25 after dipping to 126.89. Brokers said the nearest support level was still 127.00 with resistance at 128.00.

The November 2006 Btp was six basis points down at 102.90, yielding 7.44 percent and showing a spread over the benchmark Bund of 178 basis points. But the most traded July 2006 Btp was 37 basis points weaker at 107.80.

Brokers cited comments by Italian foreign minister Lamberto Dini at the weekend who said towards the end of the year Europe would be in a position to see if decisions on which countries will participate from EMU's start would need to be put back.
Bertinotti said in a newspaper interview he reckoned Prime Minister Romano Prodi's administration would not last a full five-year term -- an unprecedented feat in Italian politics.
Neither comment helped the sensitive bond market.

Bertinotti also spelled out three big difficulties in the coming months, the first unemployment and privatisation, the second Prodi's plans for a spring mini-budget and the third the full 1998 budget. "A deal on the first two is difficult and nearly impossible on the third," Bertinotti said.
Still on the domestic front the Treasury announced it would issue a total of eight trillion lire of medium to long-term paper for sale at its regular mid-month auction.
